feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED — `blocker_moved` is wrong. It must read the specific cell in front of the door and be true when that cell holds no ball (a carried ball counts as moved). Instead the candidate builds an incoherent expression (it ends in `and False`, so it can never return true) that scans the whole grid rather than the cell directly in front of the door. Fix: locate the door, compute the adjacent cell in the direction of the start room using `env.grid.get` with a `cell is not None` guard, and return true exactly when that cell holds no ball (or the ball is being carried, i.e. `env.carrying` is the ball), so that dropping the ball back in front of the door makes the predicate false again. Do not fake the event with `and False`.

CHANGES REQUIRED: The `blocker_moved` predicate is wrong. Its first disjunct `not any(cell is not None and cell.type == 'door' ...)` makes the proposition true whenever the grid contains no door (e.g. before a door scan variant, or if colors/scan fail), and the convoluted dead-code wrapper (`... if False else ...` with `dy ... if False`) is unreadable and the intended front-of-door scan is only correct if the door adjacency covers both wall sides. As written, the predicate conflates 'no door exists' with 'blocker moved', which is not the environment semantics (exactly one locked door always exists). Necessary fix: `blocker_moved` must be true exactly when (a) no cell directly adjacent to (i.e. immediately in front of, either side of the wall for) the door holds a ball, or (b) the agent carries a ball. Remove the dead-code wrapper and the 'no door exists' disjunct entirely; scan for the door cell and check the adjacent cell(s) in front of it for a ball, falling back to the carried-ball check.

NO CHANGES NEEDED. All five declared propositions have exactly one correctly named predicate, each taking env and using only allowed builtins and the documented API. blocker_moved correctly reads the current observation: it treats the ball in hand as moved and, when the ball is on the grid, checks that no cell adjacent to any door horizontally holds a ball, so it turns false again if the ball is dropped back in front of the door. has_door_key correctly requires carrying a key whose color matches a door on the grid. door_open correctly reads the current door is_open state. target_picked_up correctly requires carrying a box whose color matches the mission string, handling the variable mission color. key_lost is a proper event: it requires the previous valuation to exist (false on the first step), that has_door_key was true at the previous step, and that the key is not currently carried while the door is currently closed; it reads no RM state, reward, or state descriptions, and does not mutate env or episode_memory.
